title_ar: الشيخ الددو والدكتور عبد الحي يوسف يحاضران عن "المرأة القدوة"
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew and Dr Abd al-Hayy Yusuf Lecture on "The Exemplary Woman"
body_ar:
ألقى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو محاضرة مشتركة مع الدكتور عبد الحي يوسف نائب رئيس هيئة علماء السودان ورئيس قناة طيبة تحت عنوان: "المرأة القدوة"، وذلك في دار الشباب القديمة مساء اليوم الأربعاء 30 أكتوبر 2013م.

افتتحت المحاضرة بتلاوة آيات من الذكر الحكيم من سورة الحجرات مع إحدى القارئات.

تناول الكلام في البداية الشيخ الدكتور عبد الحي يوسف، بعد حمد الله والثناء عليه

هنأ وشكر النساء القائمات على تنظيم هذه المحاضرة ودعا لهم بالتوفيق والسداد، وذكر أنه سُرّ بما رآه من تضافر الجهود والتعاون على البر والتقوى بين الرجال والنساء لخدمة هذا الدين..

وعلق على الآيات التي تليت في افتتاح المحاضرة

مبينا أن "هذا الدين قد جاء محققا لمصالح الدنيا والآخرة ملبيا لمطالب الروح والجسد ويستوعب القضايا كلها ويحل المشاكل كلها.. وهذا يدل على شموله وسعته ومرونته..".

كما استعرض الشيخ الدكتور عبد الحي يوسف نماذج فريدة من نساء يمثلن النموذج الأعلى في القدوة، حيث تحدث عن حب خديجة لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وتضحيتها في سبيل نصرة دعوته، ومؤازرتها له في محنه..

واسترسل الشيخ الدكتور عبد الحي يوسف بذكر نماذج أخرى فريدة من الصحابيات الجليلات أمهات المؤمنين وغيرهن كثر في التاريخ الإسلامي.. ذكر منهن أم سليم والدة أنس ابن مالك رضي الله عنه.. تلك المرأة الطيبة الصالحة حين خطبها طلحة الأنصاري رضي الله عنه وهو لا يزال حينئذ كافرا.. فجعلت مهرها إسلام زوجها.. لا شيء سوى ذلك، وفيها كانت تقول عائشة أم المؤمنين رضي الله عنها: "لا أعلم امرأة كانت أكرم مهرا من أم سليم كان مهرها الإسلام".

وفي نهاية كلمته حث الدكتور عبد الحي يوسف النساء على استعادة مجد المجاهدات في صدر الإسلام، وأن يتعاونّ مع الرجال في الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر.

ثم تناول الكلام الشيخ العلامة محمد الحسن الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء الذي أكد بدوره أن هذا الموضوع ذو أهمية كبيرة، لأن الإنسان في الدنيا محاط بكثير من الفتن والشواغل وعمره قصير وجهده محدود، وهو ممتحن ومبتلى بالحياة..

وذكر الشيخ الددو أن الإنسان قد خُلق لحكمتين بالغتين ومهمتين أساسيتين لا بد للإنسان أن يترك بهما أثرا باقيا خالدا في الدنيا، وهاتان المهمتان هما: مهمة الاستخلاف في الأرض، ومهمة عبادة الله وحده.. ونبه الشيخ الددو أن الإنسان محاط بخمس جبهات كلها تحاول إغواءه فعليه أن يحترس منها.. وهذه الجبهات هي:

1- جبهة الشيطان. 2- جبهة النفس الأمارة بالسوء. 3- جبهة إخوان السوء. 4-مفاتن الحياة الدنيا. 5- نِعم الله المغدقة، وهذه الجبهات الخمس تكفي الإنسان شغلا، ولذلك احتاج الإنسان إلى القدوة الحسنة لتعينه في التغلب على هذه الجبهات.

وقد حضر المحاضرة جمهور غفير من النساء والرجال اكتظت بهم مدرجات دار الشباب القديمة، واستمرت المحاضرات التي بدأت بعد صلاة العصر بساعة إلى وقت دخول صلاة العشاء، مما اضطر الجمهور والمحاضرين إلى التوقف لصلاة المغرب واستئناف المحاضرة بعد ذلك.

نذكر في السياق ذاته أن جمعية المرأة للثقافة والتعليم هي المنظِّمة والداعية لهذه المحاضرات، ضمن مجموعة أنشطة تهدف إلى توعية النساء وتثقيفهن حول شؤون الدين والدنيا.. وتعد هذه المحاضرة هي الأولى للشيخ بعد فترة تناهز ثمانية أشهر كان قد أجرى خلالها عملية جراحية ناجحة لله الحمد، واستدعت منه أخذ فترة نقاهة استمرت ستة أشهر.
body_en:
His eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew delivered a joint lecture with Dr Abd al-Hayy Yusuf, vice-president of the Sudan Scholars Authority and head of the Taybah channel, under the title "The Exemplary Woman", at the old Youth House on the evening of today, Wednesday 30 October 2013.

The lecture opened with the recitation of verses of the Wise Remembrance from Sūrat al-Hujurat, by one of the women reciters.

The first to speak was Sheikh Dr Abd al-Hayy Yusuf. After praising God and extolling Him,

he congratulated and thanked the women who had organised this lecture and prayed for them for success and right guidance, and mentioned that he was gladdened by what he had seen of the joining of efforts and of mutual assistance in righteousness and God-consciousness (taqwā) between men and women in the service of this religion…

He commented on the verses recited at the opening of the lecture,

making clear that "this religion has come realising the benefits (maṣāliḥ) of this world and the next, answering the demands of the spirit and of the body; it takes in all questions and solves all problems… and this indicates its comprehensiveness, its breadth and its flexibility…".

Sheikh Dr Abd al-Hayy Yusuf also surveyed singular examples of women who represent the highest model of an exemplar, speaking of Khadijah's love for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of her sacrifice in support of his call, and of her standing by him in his trials…

Sheikh Dr Abd al-Hayy Yusuf went on to mention other singular examples from among the noble women Companions, the Mothers of the Believers, and many others in Islamic history. Among them he mentioned Umm Sulaym, the mother of Anas ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him — that good and righteous woman who, when Talhah al-Ansari, may God be pleased with him, proposed to her while he was at that time still an unbeliever, made her bridal gift (mahr) her husband's acceptance of Islam, and nothing besides. Of her, Aisha, Mother of the Believers, may God be pleased with her, used to say: "I know of no woman more generous in her bridal gift than Umm Sulaym: her bridal gift was Islam."

At the end of his address, Dr Abd al-Hayy Yusuf urged the women to recover the glory of the women who strove in the first age of Islam, and to co-operate with the men in enjoining right and forbidding wrong.

Then the learned Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, spoke. He affirmed for his part that this subject is of great importance, because man in this world is surrounded by many trials and preoccupations, his lifetime is short and his effort limited, and he is tested and tried by life…

Sheikh al-Dedew mentioned that man was created for two far-reaching purposes and two fundamental tasks, by which he must leave a lasting and enduring mark in this world. These two tasks are: the task of vicegerency on the earth (al-istikhlāf), and the task of worshipping God alone. Sheikh al-Dedew drew attention to the fact that man is surrounded by five fronts, all of which try to seduce him, so that he must be on his guard against them. These fronts are:

1 – the front of Satan. 2 – the front of the soul that commands to evil. 3 – the front of evil companions. 4 – the allurements of the life of this world. 5 – the abundant blessings of God. These five fronts are enough to keep a man fully occupied, and for that reason man stands in need of a good exemplar to help him overcome them.

A great crowd of women and men attended the lecture, filling the tiers of the old Youth House. The lectures, which began an hour after the afternoon prayer, continued until the time of the night prayer came in, which obliged the audience and the lecturers to break for the sunset prayer and to resume the lecture afterwards.

We note in the same connection that the Women's Association for Culture and Education is the organiser of, and the inviter to, these lectures, as part of a set of activities aimed at raising women's awareness and educating them concerning the affairs of religion and of this world… This lecture is the first by the Sheikh after a period of some eight months, during which he had undergone a successful surgical operation — praise be to God — which required him to take a period of convalescence lasting six months.

flags.arabic: صيغة الخبر الصحفي (قال فضيلة الشيخ... مؤكدا... وأضاف...)
options: render as a site news report, with the Sheikh's words marked as the site's paraphrase
render as a text by the Sheikh
flags.note: NOT A TEXT BY THE SHEIKH. This record is the site's own news write-up. Outside the passages placed in quotation marks, every formulation is the site editor's indirect report of what the Sheikh said, not his own wording, and the English preserves the reporting verbs (the Sheikh said that..., he affirmed that...) so that a reader can see this. It must not be displayed as a fatwa or as a text of his. The underlying address or lecture is not in this record.

flags.arabic: حين خطبها طلحة الأنصاري رضي الله عنه وهو لا يزال حينئذ كافرا
flags.context: Dr Abd al-Hayy Yusuf's account of Umm Sulaym's bridal gift
options: reproduce the source's name, Talhah al-Ansari, and flag it
read it as Abu Talhah al-Ansari, the Companion of the well-known account
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11). The Companion in this account is ABU Talhah al-Ansari, Zayd ibn Sahl, who married Umm Sulaym; the source drops أبو. As printed, the name reads as Talhah, which an English reader will take for Talhah ibn Ubaydullah, one of the ten given glad tidings, who is a different man and was never an unbeliever at the time of a proposal of marriage. Reproduced as printed, not silently corrected, and flagged: a wrong Companion attached to a story about accepting Islam is exactly the kind of error that must not be introduced by a translator, nor concealed.

flags.context: the first of the two tasks for which the Sheikh said man was created
options: the task of vicegerency on the earth (al-istikhlāf)
the task of stewardship of the earth
the task of succeeding one another on the earth
flags.note: istikhlāf is not in the glossary. The Qur'anic root (2:30, 'I am placing on the earth a khalīfah') supports both 'vicegerency' and, on some readings, simply 'succession' — one generation succeeding another. 'Stewardship' imports an environmental register the Arabic does not have here. Kept as the traditional 'vicegerency', with the Arabic, and flagged.

flags.arabic: تناول الكلام في البداية الشيخ الدكتور عبد الحي يوسف … ثم تناول الكلام الشيخ العلامة محمد الحسن الددو
flags.context: the structure of the whole record
options: display the record as a joint event, with each speaker's material attributed to him
display it as a text by Sheikh al-Dedew
flags.note: ATTRIBUTION. Roughly two thirds of this record reports the words of a DIFFERENT scholar, Dr Abd al-Hayy Yusuf of Sudan — including the account of Umm Sulaym, the material on Khadijah and the closing exhortation to women. Only the final third reports Sheikh al-Dedew. On a site published under the Sheikh's name, the English must keep the two apart, and the speaker's name is repeated at each turn for that reason. Neither speaker's lecture is in the corpus; this is the site's summary of both.

flags.context: the CMS timestamp on the record
options: treat as the date the item was uploaded to the CMS
treat as the date of composition
flags.note: CORPUS-WIDE DEFECT. The CMS serves a bulk-upload timestamp, not the date the Sheikh spoke or wrote. date_is_cms_upload is set true. Where the body itself names a date, that internal date is the better evidence and is kept in the English.

translator_notes: الذكر الحكيم ('the Wise Remembrance') is a name for the Qur'an; kept as the source's own epithet rather than flattened to 'the Qur'an'.
نساء يمثلن النموذج الأعلى في القدوة — القدوة is the article's keyword throughout and is rendered 'exemplar' consistently, including in the title.

المجاهدات is rendered 'the women who strove', not 'the women fighters'. The Arabic is the general jihād of effort and the context is the first generation of Muslim women in Medina; a martial English rendering would read very differently in this corpus and is not warranted by the word alone.
دار الشباب is the Maison des Jeunes, a standard Mauritanian civic venue; rendered literally as 'the Youth House'.
The five 'fronts' are numbered in the source as a run-on list inside one paragraph; the layout is preserved.
